transcript.text: Zanussi dishwasher keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in. Model ZDT21006FA

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This is a safety hazard and you must not use it until an engineer has checked it internally. The timing—tripping about 15 minutes into a cycle—is a strong clue: this is typically when the heating stage begins, suggesting the heater element may have developed an earth fault (a short to the metal casing). Less commonly, a circulation pump or internal wiring issue could cause this. To help narrow it down safely while unplugged: please check if there is water in the base of the tub and inspect the heater element at the bottom for visible damage or cracks in its insulation. Do not attempt to test it with electricity; just look for obvious signs of failure.

I've left it unplugged. I can't see any visible damage or leaks, and the floor and socket are dry. I'm not sure what the heater looks like, so I can't say about that. No burning smell either. The trip takes out the circuit with my fridge on it, so I'd like it sorted. Is this likely to need an engineer?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Yes, this is very likely to need an engineer. The fact that it trips about 15 minutes into a cycle—when the heating stage begins—is a common sign of the heater element developing an earth fault (a short circuit to the metal casing). Because this involves mains electricity and potential water ingress inside the appliance, it is not safe for a homeowner to diagnose or repair further.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.

The fault they reported is: "keeps tripping the electrics, not every time though. Usually about 15 mins in.". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
